subject: Acme Analytics — POC action plan, success gates, and SDK/streaming workback
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmeanalytics.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Acme Analytics — POC action plan, success gates, and SDK/streaming workback

Hi Samir / Laura —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a clear trial runbook and owners. TL;DR: Acme wants a 3-week POC to validate latency under 250ms p95 for short-form prompts, embedding accuracy for search re-rank, and a streaming tool-calling flow to your vector DB.

Summary of what we heard:
- Target use cases: chat+retrieval for customer support and a re-ranking pipeline for search.
- Primary success metrics: p95 gen latency < 250ms (typical prompt length ~120 tokens), embedding recall @ top-10 > current baseline, and end-to-end streaming tool-call that writes vectors to your internal store within 300ms of final token.
- Data: you will share a 10k-row redacted sample (schema attached).

Proposed POC plan and timeline (please confirm):
1) Week 0 (this week): finalize NDA + trial scope (Kimberly) — deliverable: signed PO/NDA.
2) Week 1: infra + SDK handshake — Redwood provides SDK snippets, routes, and a small streaming demo (Aditya) + Acme provides redacted sample + example prompt templates.
3) Week 2: run parallel baseline vs Redwood endpoints, collect latency/cost, and run embedding comparisons (Marissa).
4) Week 3: show findings, tweak batching/quant profiles, and agree on go/no-go.

Ownership:
- Redwood: Aditya (technical lead) / Marissa (success & metrics) / Kimberly (commercial + escalation)
- Acme: Samir (product) / Laura (data eng)

Immediate asks for you (Samir / Laura):
- Share redacted 10k sample CSV + schema by Monday EOD.
- Confirm whether streaming tool-calls must support header-level auth to your vector DB (yes/no).
- Confirm a convenient 30–45min slot for kickoff next Wednesday (propose 10am PT).

Attachments: acme-poc-action-items.xlsx (action items & timeline), streaming-sdk-snippets.md (short examples we’ll use for the SDK handshake).

Thanks — I’ll queue the internal tech prep once you confirm the kickoff time.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmeanalytics.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme Analytics — POC action plan, success gates, and SDK/streaming workback

Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear plan. A few quick confirmations from our side:
- We can share the 10k redacted sample by Monday EOD (we are running a final scrub).
- Streaming tool-call: yes, it needs to include header-level auth and an idempotency key for our ingestion endpoint. We expect the ingestion endpoint to acknowledge writes within 300ms on our side.
- Kickoff: Wednesday at 10am PT works for Samir + Laura.

One change request: can we add an integration success gate for partial-response handling? If the model streams a tool-call and then hits a network hiccup mid-stream, we need a deterministic retry/backfill path — even if it means buffering the last N tokens on the client.

We’ll also attach a short doc with our ingestion API spec before the kickoff.

Thanks,
Samir
Product Lead — Search & Knowledge
Acme Analytics

Subject: Re: Acme Analytics — POC action plan, success gates, and SDK/streaming workback

Thanks — a few technical clarifications ahead of the kickoff. I’m listing tentative implementation steps and acceptance checks so Acme and our on-call infra team align during Week 1: 

Implementation workback (high level):
1) SDK handshake (Day 1–2): provide language snippets (Python, Node) that show: auth, route selection (us-west), streaming connect + tool-call pattern, and KV-cache warmup sample. (Attachment: streaming-sdk-snippets.md)
2) Streaming tool-call contract (Day 2–4): we will implement a small proxy that streams tokens and emits a final single JSON event with the tool-call metadata. We’ll include idempotency header support and a small resumable buffer on the client SDK (configurable N tokens).
3) Embedding baseline (Day 3–7): run embedding vectors for sample set and compute recall @K vs your current system; provide a notebook with reproducible steps.
4) Load & latency tests (Day 5–12): run p95/p99 across representative prompt mixes; we’ll test with and without batching and two quantization profiles.

Acceptance checks (examples):
- Streaming tool-call arrives at Acme ingestion with correct auth header and idempotency key >= 99% of attempts under normal conditions.
- If streaming is interrupted, SDK should replay buffered tokens and complete the tool-call within 3 retry attempts without duplicating side-effects.
- P95 text-gen latency < 250ms for 120-token prompts on our dedicated trial endpoint (us-west) under nominal load (10 rps).
- Embedding recall @ top-10 >= baseline + 5% improvement OR match baseline with 30% lower cost.

Open questions for kickoff:
- Samir: what auth scheme do you want for ingestion? Bearer token, mTLS, or HMAC?
- Laura: can you confirm the ingestion endpoint SLA for writes (300ms target) and whether there are burst limits we need to model?

I’ll prepare a short demo that shows a streaming model -> tool-call -> ingestion with idempotency next Wednesday.

—Aditya
Senior Engineer, Inference Integrations | Redwood Inference
